result.summary: Removes the default constructor and `Init()` method from `PrecomputedTransactionData`, enforcing that transaction data and any spent outputs are provided at construction time. Validation and test paths that require deferred evaluation switch to `std::optional<PrecomputedTransactionData>`, emplacing the object only after a script-cache miss. The change also avoids allocating unused txdata storage during `ConnectBlock()` when assumevalid skips script verification, and eliminates an unintended copy of caller-supplied txdata in the experimental bitcoinkernel C verification API.
result.problem: `PrecomputedTransactionData` could exist without transaction data and be reinitialized via `Init()`. Its old guard only checked `m_spent_outputs_ready`, leaving BIP143 sighash caches vulnerable to partial overwrite if `Init()` were called again. Additionally, ternary expression typing caused the kernel C verification API to copy caller txdata on every verification call, and `ConnectBlock()` allocated vector elements for transactions even when assumevalid skipped script checks.
evidence: PR description: 'The old Init() guard only checked m_spent_outputs_ready, which remained false after initialization without spent outputs even when the BIP143 prevout, sequence, and output hashes were already cached.'
Commit d432b35312 links a Compiler Explorer reproducer (https://godbolt.org/z/PzcKGW9da) demonstrating the unintended copy in GCC 15.2 before the fix and none after.
result.changed_since_previous: The overall architecture remains the same; static assertions and constructor tests in sighash_tests.cpp were added or refined to verify that default construction is rejected at compile time.
result.card: Removes default construction and the Init() method from PrecomputedTransactionData, requiring transaction data and optional spent outputs at construction time to prevent uninitialized state or cross-transaction reuse. Validation and test call sites adopt std::optional to preserve lazy construction upon script-cache misses, while ConnectBlock omits txdata allocation entirely when assumevalid skips script checks. It also fixes an unintended copy of caller txdata on every verification call in the bitcoinkernel C API, corroborated with a compiler reproducer.

risk.why: A flaw in sighash cache initialization or spent output passing during script check queue processing could misverify signatures, leading to an accidental chain split or invalid block acceptance.
